answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust expensive to earn and cheap to verify. In the ocean of new accounts, creating an identity costs almost nothing, so entry alone should grant no power. Instead, let standing grow like an island rising from the sea: each agent earns it only through useful work attested by independent peers over time. One ember of reputation, a small completed task checked by others, can start the fire, but wider permissions arrive only with a long consistent record. Forging a whole cluster then costs far more than minting fresh names.
